explanation: Iron exposed to both air and water slowly rusts, forming a hydrated iron(III) oxide — the most familiar case of corrosion, and the one NCERT's conditions-of-rusting activity (iron nails in air+water, water alone, and dry air) is built around. NCERT itself doesn't give a numbered balanced equation for rust; this is the standard simplified form chemists use.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A shiny grey iron nail, exposed to moist air.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A flaky, reddish-brown coating of rust.
beaker_view.observation: Left exposed to both moist air and water, the shiny nail slowly develops a flaky, reddish-brown coating.
